newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday May 14.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Prime Minister Romano Prodi, flanked by senior cabinet ministers, met union leaders for the first round of talks over welfare reforms in what promises to be a lengthy negotiation process (all).

* Sergio D'Antoni, the head of Cisl union federation, after a meeting with Prodi, said unions were not ready to discuss cuts in welfare state spending before the government prepared the outline of its latest DPEF, the three-year economic programme (all).

* Separatist Northern League leader Umberto Bossi made an overture to the government by announcing he would today hold talks with Massimo D'Alema, the head of a parliamentary commission aimed at studying costitutional reforms (all).

* Italian producer prices rose 0.9 percent year-on year in March and 0.3 percent month-on-month, Istat figures showed. Wholesale prices for March showed an increase of 0.3 percent on a year basis and a fall of 0.2 percent on a month basis (all).

* In an interview with French business daily la Tribune released on Monday, Prodi warned if the lira was left out of a single European currency in 1999 the reaction of financial markets would be impossible to control. Prodi also said the country was determined to use all political instruments at its disposal to ensure the lira joined EMU.
* Cement producer Unicem said a 20.5 percent stake in the company currently held by Agnelli family holding Ifil will be sold to Fratelli Buzzi at 18,800 lire a share (all).
* French group Canal Plus and German media company Kirch are
reportedly close to an agreement to sell the German group's 45
percent stake in Italy's pay TV Telepiu' (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
